comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C18-C25 regarding Drice expression patterns and characterization in adult brains. Both evaluations find the western blot, histochemical, and knockdown data convincing with no concerns raised.

Perfect agreement on claims C37-C39 regarding negative co-IP results and substrate cleavage assays. Both evaluations accept these findings as part of the mechanistic characterization without challenge.

Perfect agreement on claims C7, C70-C75 regarding behavioral effects of Fas3G overexpression. While peer reviewers initially requested clarification, they ultimately accepted the results as convincing after revisions.

Strong agreement on claims C2, C3, C26-C29 regarding TurboID proximity labeling and membrane localization of Drice. Peer review also includes C77 (exclusive sequestration claim). Both find the proximity labeling approach and GO analysis convincing.

Strong agreement on claims C5, C6, C58-C62 regarding Dronc recruitment and requirement for caspase activation. Both evaluations find the mechanistic data convincing, with peer reviewers noting thorough responses to concerns.

Strong agreement on claims C54-C56 regarding Fas3G knockdown showing non-essentiality for basal activation. Peer review explicitly acknowledges the negative results and redundant mechanisms interpretation.

Strong agreement on claims C8, C76, C78 regarding the central mechanistic model of membrane sequestration enabling non-lethal activation. Both evaluations find this interpretation convincing and timely.
Strong agreement on claims C30, C33-C36 regarding isoform-specific identification of Fas3G. Both evaluations accept the proximity labeling and antibody validation without concerns about methodology.

Strong agreement on claims C4, C50-C53 regarding non-lethal caspase activation upon Fas3G overexpression. Both evaluations find the MASCaT data and controls convincing. Peer review also includes C48, C57.

Agreement on claim C40 regarding MASCaT reporter development. Both evaluations explicitly affirm the utility and validation of this new tool, with peer reviewers praising the sophisticated techniques.

Partial overlap on claims C44-C47 regarding differential effects of Drice vs. Dcp-1 overexpression. Peer review R11 covers broader mechanistic findings including these claims. Both evaluations support the cell counting data.

Partial overlap on claims C65-C66 regarding differential outcomes of Dronc overexpression methods. Peer review R11 includes these as part of broader mechanistic characterization. Both evaluations accept these findings.

OpenEval evaluated claims C1, C9-C17 as background knowledge supported by literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers typically do not explicitly evaluate background claims.

OpenEval evaluated claims C31, C67-C69, C79-C88 as literature-supported contextual claims. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these represent discussion and background rather than primary experimental findings.

OpenEval evaluated claims C89-C90 as speculative statements about future applications and reversibility. No corresponding peer review evaluation found. OpenEval notes these are hypotheses rather than demonstrated results.
